translationRepairs: He gave battle, shattered Fu Deng, and left two-thirds of the enemy dying of thirst; that night Fu Deng's army melted away and he fled to Yong.
He gave battle, shattered Fu Deng, and left two or three tenths of the enemy dying of thirst; that night Fu Deng's army melted away and he fled to Yong.
十二三 is two or three parts in ten, not two-thirds.
Fu Deng had left Fu Guang at Yong and crown prince Fu Chong at Hu Kong; both bolted when they heard of his defeat.
Fu Deng had left Fu Guang at Yong and his son Fu Chong at Hu Kong; both bolted when they heard of his defeat.
The sentence names 子崇, Fu Deng's son Chong, and does not call him crown prince.
He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and other generals as dukes or marquises.
He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Jing together with meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others as dukes or marquises.
征南靖 is a named general Jing omitted from the idiomatic sentence.
He posthumously titled his stepmother Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.
He posthumously titled his concubine-mother Lady Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.
庶母 is Xing's concubine-mother Lady Sun, not a stepmother.
Fu Deng still lives; civil war would repeat the Yuan brothers' folly and hand victory away.
Fu Deng still lives; civil war would repeat the folly of the two Yuans and hand victory away.
二袁 means the two Yuans and does not call Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu brothers.
He summoned Ru to be Director of the Secretariat.
He summoned Ru to be a minister of the Secretariat.
尚書 is a Secretariat ministership, not 尚書令, Director of the Secretariat.
When Murong Yong fell, Liu Gong of Hedong and others held out until Yao Xing sent Yao Xu.
After Murong Yong had been destroyed by Murong Chui, Liu Gong of Hedong and others held out until Yao Xing sent Yao Xu.
慕容永既為慕容垂所滅 names Murong Chui as the agent who destroyed Murong Yong.
Xue Qiang held Yang's redoubt and guided Yao Xu across at Longmen into Puyang.
Xue Qiang held Yang's redoubt and guided Yao Xu across at Longmen into Puban.
蒲阪 is Puban; Puyang is a different place, and the next sentence already uses Puban.
The General Who Guards the East Xue Qiang first held Yang's fort, led Xu from Longmen to cross the river, and thereupon entered Puyang.
The General Who Guards the East Xue Qiang first held Yang's fort, led Xu from Longmen to cross the river, and thereupon entered Puban.
The literal field likewise mistranslates 蒲阪 as Puyang.
Xue Bo fled beyond the passes; Hu of Shang and Ercheng joined him and besieged Yao Xiang at Jincheng.
Xue Bo fled beyond the passes; Hu of Shang commandery and Erchuan joined him and besieged Yao Xiang at Jincheng.
貳川 is Erchuan, distinct from earlier 貳城 (Ercheng).
Yao Chong failed at Jinyong against Xiahou Zongzhi but sacked Baigu and deported twenty thousand refugee families.
Yao Chong failed at Jinyong against Xiahou Zongzhi but sacked Baigu and moved more than twenty thousand refugee households of Xihe Yan Yan, Hedong Pei Qi, Han Xi, and others, then returned.
The Chinese names the refugee leaders 嚴彥、裴岐、韓襲, whom the idiomatic sentence drops.
Elder scholars such as Jiang Kan, Chunyu Qi, and Gao Guo taught thousands of students in Chang'an.
Elder scholars such as Jiang Kan, Chunyu Qi, and Guo Gao taught in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
郭高 is Guo Gao, and 萬數千 is more than ten thousand students from afar, not a reversed name teaching mere thousands.

Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Gao Guo of Fengyi, and others were all aged Confucians of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, each with several hundred disciples, teaching in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.

Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were all aged Confucians of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, each with several hundred disciples, teaching in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
The literal field reverses 郭高 as Gao Guo.
Hu Bian of Liangzhou had fled to Luoyang with a thousand pupils; Guanzhong students flocked to him.
Hu Bian of Liangzhou, at the end of Fu Jian's time, moved east to Luoyang and lectured to more than a thousand disciples; many later students of Guanzhong went to him to seek instruction.
